counties.name: Palm Beach County
counties.imgAlt: Freshly groomed black and white doodle in a pink flamingo bandana
intro: The Pet-Stetician brings stress-free mobile dog grooming to homes across Palm Beach County, from Tequesta and Jupiter in the north to Boynton Beach in the south and Wellington in the west. Julia grooms every dog one-on-one in a fully equipped grooming van parked right outside your home.

sections.h2: Why mobile grooming makes sense in Palm Beach County
p: Palm Beach County is big, and traffic on I-95 and the main roads can turn a salon drop-off into a half-day errand. Mobile grooming skips all of that. There’s no drive, no drop-off window, no cage, and no long wait for pickup. Your dog is groomed close to home and is back inside as soon as they’re done.
It’s calmer for your dog, too. With no other dogs around and one groomer focused entirely on them, nervous dogs, seniors, and puppies tend to feel much more relaxed.

faq.q: Do you offer mobile dog grooming everywhere in Palm Beach County?
faq.a: We groom across Palm Beach County, including West Palm Beach, Palm Beach Gardens, Jupiter, Wellington, Boynton Beach, Lake Worth, Royal Palm Beach, North Palm Beach, Juno Beach, Tequesta, and everywhere in between. Not sure if you’re in range? Call or text 973.896.4547 and just ask.

With mobile grooming there’s no car ride and no waiting room. Your dog is groomed one-on-one with premium, pet-safe products and handed back to you clean, happy, and looking their best.

cities.name: West Palm Beach
cities.imgAlt: Freshly groomed merle doodle with a blue eye and pastel bandana
cities.intro: West Palm Beach is the county seat and the biggest city in Palm Beach County, and it’s right in the heart of our service area. Julia brings her fully equipped grooming van to your home, from the historic neighborhoods north of downtown to the newer communities out west, so your dog is groomed one-on-one without a trip to a busy salon.
cities.h2: Grooming tips for West Palm Beach dogs
p: City dogs here deal with hot pavement, humid afternoons, and plenty of walks along the waterfront. Regular brushing and a bath every few weeks keep coats from matting in the humidity, and a neat trim around the paw pads helps your dog keep traction on tile and sidewalks.

Live in a condo or townhome? Mention your building and parking situation when you book so we can plan where the van parks. The groom happens inside the van, so the main thing we need is a spot close to your door.

faq.q: Can you groom my dog if I live in a West Palm Beach condo?
faq.a: In most cases, yes. The groom happens inside the van, so we just need a place to park close to your building. Let us know about any parking or guest rules when you book, or call 973.896.4547 if you’re unsure.

cities.name: Palm Beach Gardens
cities.imgAlt: Freshly groomed golden retriever in a blue gingham bandana
cities.intro: From the neighborhoods off PGA Boulevard to the golf and gated communities to the west, Palm Beach Gardens is a natural fit for mobile grooming. Your dog stays close to home, gets Julia’s full attention, and skips the car ride and the kennel wait.
cities.h2: Gated community? Here’s how it works
p: Many Palm Beach Gardens neighborhoods have a guard gate or a guest list. When you book, add The Pet-Stetician as an expected visitor and note any gate instructions so Julia can pull right up to your home on time.

Gardens dogs spend lots of time on manicured lawns and golf-course paths, which means grass seeds, sticky paws, and coats that pick up everything. A tidy paw trim and a regular brush-out make a big difference between full grooms.

faq.q: Can you come to a gated community in Palm Beach Gardens?
faq.a: Yes. Just add us to your gate or guest list and put any access instructions in your booking notes so Julia can get straight to your door.

cities.name: Jupiter
cities.imgAlt: Freshly groomed tan and white puppy in a beach bandana
cities.intro: Jupiter dogs live the good life: beach walks, boat days, and long afternoons outside. The Pet-Stetician brings the grooming van to your Jupiter home so your pup gets cleaned up one-on-one, right in your driveway.
cities.h2: Beach dogs need a little extra care
p: Sand, salt water, and sun are hard on a coat. Salt can dry out skin and fur, and sand works its way down to the skin and between the toes. If your dog loves the dog beach along A1A, a fresh bath and thorough brush-out every few weeks keeps their coat soft and their skin comfortable.
Rinsing your dog with fresh water after the beach helps between appointments. Julia can also suggest a grooming schedule and a coat length that’s easier to keep clean through the summer.

faq.q: How often should a Jupiter beach dog be groomed?
faq.a: Dogs that swim or play in the sand often do best on the shorter end of the usual 4–8 week schedule, with a fresh-water rinse at home after beach days. Julia can recommend the right timing for your dog’s coat.

p: Dogs that hang out at the barn tend to collect dirt, shavings, burrs, and the occasional surprise in their coat. A deep-clean bath and full brush-out gets them back to fresh, and keeping their coat at a practical length makes the weeks between grooms much easier.
Because the van comes to you, it’s easy to fit a groom in around lessons, shows, and busy family schedules. Just let us know where to park when you book.

faq.q: Can you groom my dog at a Wellington horse property?
faq.a: As long as there’s a place for the van to park near you, yes. Add your address and any gate or parking notes when you book, or call 973.896.4547 to check.

cities.h2: Easier grooming for dogs of every age

faq.q: Is mobile grooming good for nervous small dogs?

cities.h2: Grooming that fits a family schedule
p: Between school runs, sports, and work, finding time to drop a dog off at a salon and pick them up hours later is hard. With mobile grooming there’s no drop-off window and no waiting; your dog is groomed one-on-one in the van and handed back clean and happy.
Kids and dogs mean muddy paws and backyard adventures. Regular baths, nail trims, and ear cleaning keep family dogs comfortable, and your couch a little cleaner.

p: Dogs that swim, ride on the boat, or play by the water can end up with damp coats that stay humid and start to tangle or smell. A thorough bath, dry, and brush-out resets the coat, and regular ear cleaning matters for dogs who spend a lot of time in the water.
Julia can help you choose a coat length and grooming schedule that work with your dog’s time on the water.

faq.q: Why does ear cleaning matter for dogs that swim?
faq.a: Moisture trapped in the ears can lead to buildup and irritation. Gentle, regular ear cleaning as part of a groom helps keep ears clean. If you notice redness, odor, or lots of scratching, check with your vet.

p: Salty air and sandy walks are part of life in Juno Beach. Regular baths and brush-outs keep salt and sand from drying out your dog’s skin, and a paw tidy keeps sand from collecting between the toes.
Book online any time, or call or text 973.896.4547 to find a time that works for you.

faq.q: What’s the best haircut for a Florida beach dog?
faq.a: It depends on the coat. Many curly and doodle coats are easier to keep clean in a shorter summer trim, but double-coated breeds like goldens and huskies usually shouldn’t be shaved, since their coat helps protect them from heat and sun. Julia will recommend what suits your dog.

faq.q: How do I keep my dog’s coat from matting between grooms?
faq.a: Brush a few times a week, paying extra attention behind the ears, under the legs, and around the collar, where mats start first. Regular grooms every 4–8 weeks keep the coat manageable.

services.name: Bath & Brush
services.short: Deep clean, condition, and brush-out for a soft, fresh coat.
services.imgAlt: Freshly groomed white bichon in a yellow daisy bandana
services.quick: A mobile bath & brush is a deep-clean bath, conditioning, and full brush-out, done in The Pet-Stetician’s grooming van parked right outside your home in Palm Beach, Martin, or St. Lucie County. It’s a great way to keep your dog fresh and comfortable between haircuts.

sections.h2: What a bath & brush is for
p: A bath & brush is about a clean, healthy coat rather than a new haircut. It’s a great fit for short-coated dogs, for dogs between haircuts, and for any pup who’s been rolling in something they shouldn’t have.

ul: Short-coated breeds like Labs, beagles, and boxers
Dogs who are between full haircuts
Beach and pool dogs who need salt, chlorine, and sand washed out
Senior dogs who do best with a simpler, gentler visit

p: Combine a bath & brush with de-shedding, nail trimming, or ear cleaning for a more complete refresh. If your dog needs a new look too, book haircuts & styling instead.

faq.q: How often should my dog have a professional bath?
faq.a: Most dogs do well with a professional bath every 4–8 weeks, depending on coat and lifestyle. Dogs who swim or play outside a lot may need one more often.

faq.q: Is a bath & brush the same as a full groom?
faq.a: No. A bath & brush focuses on cleaning, conditioning, and brushing the coat. If your dog also needs a haircut or style, book haircuts & styling instead.

services.name: Haircuts & Styling
services.short: Breed-standard or custom styles that suit your pet perfectly.
services.imgAlt: Freshly groomed merle doodle with a blue eye and pastel bandana
services.quick: Mobile dog haircuts & styling from The Pet-Stetician means a breed-standard or custom cut, done one-on-one by Julia in a fully equipped grooming van at your home. Every style is tailored to your dog’s coat, lifestyle, and your preferences.

p: Some pet parents want the classic breed look; others want something practical for Florida weather, or just plain cute. Tell Julia what you like, share a photo if you have one, and she’ll tailor the cut to your dog’s coat type and temperament.

Curly and wavy coats keep growing and mat quickly in humidity, so they need regular haircuts. Doodles, poodles, bichons, shih tzus, schnauzers, and other low-shedding breeds usually do best on a steady schedule.

sections.h2: A note on shaving double coats
p: Double-coated breeds like goldens, shepherds, and huskies usually shouldn’t be shaved down, because their coat helps regulate temperature and protect their skin from the sun. For these dogs, de-shedding and a tidy trim are usually the better choice.

faq.q: How often does my dog need a haircut?
faq.a: Most dogs with growing coats, like doodles, poodles, and shih tzus, do well with a haircut every 4–8 weeks. Julia can recommend a schedule based on your dog’s coat and the length you like.

faq.q: What should I tell the groomer before a haircut?
faq.a: Your preferred length and style, any problem areas, and anything about your dog’s temperament, health, or sensitive spots. You can add notes when you book online.

services.name: De-Shedding
services.short: Reduce shedding and keep your home (and pup) fur-free.
services.imgAlt: Freshly groomed golden retriever in a blue gingham bandana
services.quick: De-shedding is a bath and thorough brush-out that removes loose undercoat before it ends up on your floors and furniture. The Pet-Stetician does it one-on-one in a mobile grooming van at your home in Palm Beach, Martin, and St. Lucie Counties.

sections.h2: Why Florida dogs shed so much
p: Many dogs blow their coat seasonally, but in Florida’s warm climate shedding can feel like it never stops. Double-coated breeds hold onto a dense undercoat that, if it isn’t removed, traps heat and moisture against the skin.

ul: German shepherds, huskies, and other double-coated breeds
Corgis, Australian shepherds, and herding breeds
Any dog leaving tumbleweeds of fur around the house

sections.h2: Keeping shedding under control at home
p: Brushing a few times a week with the right brush for your dog’s coat, plus a professional de-shed every 4–8 weeks, keeps the undercoat from building up. Ask Julia which brush suits your dog.

faq.q: Should I shave my double-coated dog to stop shedding?
faq.a: Usually not. A double coat helps protect your dog from heat and sun, and shaving can affect how it grows back. Regular de-shedding removes the loose undercoat without taking away that protection.

faq.q: How often should I book de-shedding?
faq.a: Every 4–8 weeks is typical, and more often during heavy shedding seasons.

services.name: Puppy Grooming
services.short: Positive, patient first grooms to build lifelong comfort.
services.imgAlt: Freshly groomed tan and white puppy in a beach bandana
services.quick: Puppy grooming at The Pet-Stetician is a gentle, patient introduction to bathing, brushing, and nail trims, done one-on-one in a mobile grooming van at your home. Grooming close to home, with no cages or barking dogs, helps puppies grow up comfortable with grooming.

p: A puppy’s first grooming experiences shape how they feel about grooming for life. Positive, unhurried early visits help them get used to being handled, bathed, dried, and brushed, which makes every future groom easier for everyone.

sections.h2: Why mobile grooming is great for puppies
ul: No car ride to a strange place
No cages and no waiting with other dogs
One groomer, one puppy, full attention

p: Gently handle your puppy’s paws, ears, and face every day, and keep short brushing sessions positive with treats. These small habits make real grooms much easier.

faq.q: When should my puppy have their first groom?
faq.a: Check with your vet about vaccines and timing, then book a gentle first groom. Starting early with short, positive visits helps puppies get comfortable with grooming.

faq.q: What happens at a puppy’s first groom?
faq.a: The focus is on making grooming a good experience: a gentle bath, brushing, and a nail trim as your puppy is comfortable, with plenty of patience along the way.
